Recreate the attached study notebook photo with a materially more ordinary, believable phone-photo appearance. Image is content reference, NOT style to imitate. Keep its exact educational text, an open notebook on desk and a single real physical pen beside it. Portrait 3:4 target1080x1440.

Primary fixes: replace the reference's deliberately formed heavy calligraphy, ornate sneaker/anatomy drawing and uniformly textured paper. It needs to look like notes an ordinary person actually wrote for themselves, photographed while studying.

An inexpensive A5 school notebook opened on a plain light gray-beige laminate desk with extremely subtle wear, no dramatic woodgrain. The page is smooth ordinary white notebook paper with thin faint blue-grey horizontal rules, not rough watercolor paper. Notebook a little skewed, near-overhead smartphone shot slightly off center, focus sharp on the written page, subtly softer far corner, natural soft window light from left with physically consistent gentle shadows at binding and underneath pen. Some very faint reverse-side ink show-through and a small natural page bend only, no artificial stains, film grain, distressed textures, decorative clutter or heavy photographic filter. Slightly imperfect framing but all required text fully in frame.
Open notebook covers 82% of width; a slim portion of left page and stitched binding visible. An ordinary unbranded black plastic retractable ballpoint pen (single push button, one clip, simple consistent construction) lies diagonally on exposed desk to the right with a narrow contact shadow. Scale physically plausible: pen length roughly 60% of notebook page height, not oversized. Entire pen visible, not overlapping notes. It should feel casually put down, not a stationery product arrangement.

Handwriting absolutely critical: ordinary Chinese adult daily quick HARD-PEN writing, not calligraphy. Dark blue 0.5mm ballpoint ink, mostly uniform narrow line with subtle pressure differences, occasional strokes connect naturally. Characters have distinctly variable width and tilt; repeated characters are not clones. NO brush-like flared ends, no exaggerated sharp angular calligraphy, no neatly spaced imitation handwriting font. English casual legible fast pen writing, modest joining, slightly varying slant. Heading written a little larger and more firmly, about 1.6x English/body, but with SAME thin pen, never brush or marker. More convincing pen handwriting, not merely more noise.
Visual hierarchy keeps thumbnail attraction: two-line question at upper quarter, tiny quick diagram in middle, full A/B phrases clearly visible in lower third. Natural slightly uneven spacing and indentation, no mechanically aligned perfect halves. Title reads:
鞋还没坏，
怎么就穿不了了？
A SINGLE quick blue underline under 没坏; one restrained pale yellow short highlight under 穿不了了. No red ink, no multiple decorative strokes.

Middle diagram: replace detailed foot/sneaker illustration with VERY SIMPLE 10-second learner doodles, a generic bare foot side outline above a shorter intact shoe outline, both face right and heel-aligned. Foot clearly 25% longer. Use only a handful of pen lines, shoe has no precise seams, stitching, texture or shading; at most two lace loops. Foot has no anatomical shading, toenails or tendons. No hatching. Short imperfect dashed guide at heels. Small casual annotations:
脚长大了 (arrow to foot)
鞋还好好的 (arrow to smaller intact shoe)
Diagram uses only about 20% of page, functional not polished.

Lower area: two handwritten vocabulary entries, natural slightly staggered positions, full phrase on own line. Text:
grow out of
长大后穿不下
wear out
穿久了，把鞋穿坏
Gloss for wear out wraps into two lines so text does not crowd edge. English similar size to the question's secondary line, mobile readable. Keep all text at least8% from image sides and10% from image bottom. No extra text, no watermark or brand. No new objects. Maintain accurate characters and grammar. This is AI-simulated imagery, do not write authenticity claims. Preserve the appeal of a useful note someone might save, with the physical notebook and pen convincing as ordinary objects.
